decisions.reason: Floor-level shower drainage remains strategically important, but after several years and no clear website presence the specific 2018 line has likely revealed its value and is more likely to be replaced or folded into newer core systems than kept as a separate option.

Although it was launched as a flagship designer line, two years without observed visibility suggest the original 2018 product has probably yielded its learning value and can be discontinued in favor of successor designs within the same strategic direction.

This integrated shower element is complementary rather than indispensable, and with time the firm has likely learned enough about demand to reallocate resources away from a less visible supporting option.

The basement drain solved a clear niche problem, but its weaker fit with the firm's main future emphasis and lack of later visibility make withdrawal within the next year more likely than continued commitment.

The air-admittance valve appears the most peripheral to the firm's core design-led drainage trajectory, so after an extended market test management would likely close this option and free resources for stronger lines and new development.
